question_en: At which Harappan site was a dockyard discovered, showing the civilisation's sea trade?
explanation_en: Lothal in Gujarat (excavated by S. R. Rao) has a brick dockyard. It linked Harappan trade with West Asia.

question_en: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir under the patronage of which ruler?
explanation_en: The Fourth Council met at Kundalvana in Kashmir under Kanishka, presided over by Vasumitra. Buddhism split into Hinayana and Mahayana after it.

question_en: Which of Ashoka's edicts describes the Kalinga War and his remorse over it?
explanation_en: Major Rock Edict XIII records the Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE) and Ashoka's turn to Dhamma. It also mentions Greek kings to whom envoys were sent.

question_en: The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription) praising Samudragupta was composed by:
explanation_en: Harisena, court poet of Samudragupta, composed the Prayaga Prashasti. It lists Samudragupta's conquests in north and south India.

question_en: The three Sangam assemblies of Tamil poets were held under the patronage of which dynasty?
explanation_en: Tradition says the three Sangams were held at Madurai and nearby under Pandya kings. Sangam literature is the main source for early Tamil history.

question_en: Which is the correct chronological order of the dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate?
explanation_en: The Sultanate ran from the Mamluks (1206) to the Khaljis, Tughluqs, Sayyids and Lodis. It ended when Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526.

question_en: Which Delhi Sultan introduced token currency, issuing bronze/copper coins to be valued at par with silver coins?
explanation_en: Muhammad bin Tughluq issued token coins around 1329–30. The scheme failed because the coins were easily forged, and it was withdrawn.

question_en: Which Sultan set up the Diwan-i-Khairat, a department to help the poor and arrange marriages of their daughters?
explanation_en: Firoz Shah Tughluq created the Diwan-i-Khairat (charity) and a separate department of slaves. He is also known for canals and new towns such as Hisar.

question_en: In the Second Battle of Panipat (1556), Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan defeated:
explanation_en: In 1556 Akbar's army led by Bairam Khan defeated Hemu, the general of Adil Shah Sur. The victory secured Mughal rule in north India.

question_en: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar to commemorate his victory over:
explanation_en: Akbar built the Buland Darwaza to mark his conquest of Gujarat (1573). It is the main gateway of the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri.

question_en: 'Amuktamalyada', a Telugu work on statecraft and devotion, was written by which Vijayanagar ruler?
explanation_en: Krishnadeva Raya of the Tuluva dynasty wrote Amuktamalyada in Telugu. His court had the eight poets known as the Ashtadiggajas.

question_en: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674 at which fort?
explanation_en: Shivaji's coronation took place at Raigad in June 1674. Raigad served as the Maratha capital after that.

question_en: The Adi Granth was compiled in 1604 by which Sikh Guru?
explanation_en: Guru Arjan Dev, the fifth Guru, compiled the Adi Granth and installed it at Harmandir Sahib. Guru Gobind Singh later declared the Granth the eternal Guru.

question_en: The Second Anglo-Mysore War ended with which treaty between Tipu Sultan and the English in 1784?
explanation_en: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) restored mutual conquests and ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War. The Treaty of Madras ended the first war and Seringapatam (1792) the third.

question_en: Who commanded the East India Company's army in the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
explanation_en: Major Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II at Buxar. The victory led to the grant of Diwani in 1765.

question_en:
Match the Governors-General with the measures of their time:
(a) Lord Cornwallis  (b) Lord William Bentinck  (c) Lord Dalhousie  (d) Lord Ripon
(i) Local self-government resolution  (ii) First railway line  (iii) Abolition of Sati  (iv) Permanent Settlement
explanation_en: Cornwallis brought the Permanent Settlement (1793), Bentinck abolished Sati (1829), Dalhousie opened the first railway (1853) and Ripon passed the local self-government resolution (1882).

question_en: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced by which Act?
explanation_en: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms) gave Muslims separate electorates. Lord Minto was the Viceroy at the time.

question_en: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow?
explanation_en: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt in Lucknow (Awadh). Rani Lakshmibai led at Jhansi, Kunwar Singh in Bihar and Nana Saheb at Kanpur.

question_en: The Satyashodhak Samaj (1873), which worked for the rights of lower castes, was founded by:
explanation_en: Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune in 1873. He also wrote 'Gulamgiri' against caste oppression.

question_en: The Santhal Rebellion (Hul) of 1855–56 was led by:
explanation_en: Brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu led the Santhal Hul against zamindars, moneylenders and the British. The Santhal Parganas district was created after it.

question_en: The 'Purna Swaraj' resolution was adopted by the Congress at which session, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru?
explanation_en: The Lahore session of December 1929 adopted Purna Swaraj as the goal. 26 January 1930 was then observed as Independence Day.

question_en: Gandhiji undertook his first hunger strike in India during which movement?
explanation_en: Gandhiji fasted during the Ahmedabad mill strike (1918) to support the workers' wage demand. Champaran was his first civil disobedience in India.

question_en: The Kakori train action of 1925 was carried out by members of which organisation?
explanation_en: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan and others of the HRA looted the train at Kakori. In 1928 the HRA became the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.

question_en: Who chaired the Boundary Commissions that drew the India–Pakistan border in 1947?
explanation_en: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions. The 'Radcliffe Line' was made public on 17 August 1947.

question_en: Which was the first state formed on a linguistic basis, in 1953?
explanation_en: Andhra State was created on 1 October 1953 after Potti Sriramulu died on fast. This led to the States Reorganisation Commission under Fazl Ali.

question_en: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926–2004) was a famous exponent of which classical dance?
explanation_en: Kelucharan Mohapatra revived and popularised Odissi of Odisha. He received the Padma Vibhushan in 2000.

question_en: Sattriya, recognised as a classical dance, originated in the monasteries of which state?
explanation_en: Sattriya was introduced by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev in the sattras (monasteries) of Assam. The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognised it as classical in 2000.

question_en:
Match the folk dances with their states:
(a) Lavani  (b) Giddha  (c) Ghoomar  (d) Bihu
(i) Assam  (ii) Rajasthan  (iii) Punjab  (iv) Maharashtra
explanation_en: Lavani is from Maharashtra, Giddha from Punjab, Ghoomar from Rajasthan and Bihu from Assam. Folk dances by state are a regular DSSSB topic.

question_en: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a renowned player of which instrument?
explanation_en: Amjad Ali Khan is a sarod maestro of the Senia Bangash gharana. He received the Padma Vibhushan in 2001.

question_en: The Sun Temple at Konark was built by Narasimhadeva I of which dynasty?
explanation_en: Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty built Konark in the 13th century. It is shaped as the Sun god's chariot and is a UNESCO site.

question_en: The rock-cut Kailasa temple (Cave 16) at Ellora was built under which dynasty?
explanation_en: Rashtrakuta king Krishna I built the Kailasa temple, carved from a single rock. Ellora has Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves.

question_en: The Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2021, is located in:
explanation_en: The Ramappa Temple at Palampet in Mulugu district, Telangana was built under the Kakatiyas. It was inscribed in 2021, the same year as Dholavira.

question_en: The Hornbill Festival, held every December, is celebrated in which state?
explanation_en: The Hornbill Festival is held at Kisama near Kohima, Nagaland from 1 to 10 December. It showcases the culture of the Naga tribes.

question_en: 'Bani Thani', often called the Indian Mona Lisa, belongs to which school of painting?
explanation_en: Bani Thani was painted by Nihal Chand in the Kishangarh school of Rajasthan under Raja Sawant Singh. A postage stamp on it was issued in 1973.

question_en: 'Mudrarakshasa', a Sanskrit play about Chandragupta Maurya's rise to power, was written by:
explanation_en: Vishakhadatta wrote Mudrarakshasa, which shows Chanakya's plans against the Nanda minister Rakshasa. Shudraka wrote Mrichchhakatika.

question_en: Who presided over the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946 as its temporary President?
explanation_en: Dr Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was temporary President. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.

question_en: The Objectives Resolution, which later became the basis of the Preamble, was moved in the Constituent Assembly by:
explanation_en: Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946 and it was adopted on 22 January 1947. Its ideals were reflected in the Preamble.

question_en:
Match the features of the Constitution with their sources:
(a) Judicial review  (b) Directive Principles  (c) Fundamental Duties  (d) Concurrent List
(i) Australia  (ii) USSR  (iii) Ireland  (iv) USA
explanation_en: Judicial review came from the USA, DPSP from Ireland, Fundamental Duties from the former USSR and the Concurrent List from Australia.

question_en: Which Schedule of the Constitution lists the 22 recognised languages?
explanation_en: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages. The last four (Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali) were added by the 92nd Amendment in 2003.

question_en: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form?
explanation_en: Article 17 abolishes untouchability, and its practice is an offence punishable by law. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 gives effect to it.

question_en: Employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or other hazardous work is prohibited by:
explanation_en: Article 24 is part of the Right against Exploitation. Article 23 bans human trafficking and forced labour.

question_en:
Consider the statements:
I. Fundamental Rights are justiciable, while Directive Principles cannot be enforced by any court.
II. Directive Principles are contained in Part III of the Constitution.
Which is/are correct?
explanation_en: Article 37 says DPSPs are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental in governance. DPSPs are in Part IV; Part III contains the Fundamental Rights.

question_en: The Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment on the recommendation of which committee?
explanation_en: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended Fundamental Duties, added as Part IV-A (Article 51A). The Verma Committee (1999) later studied their implementation.

question_en: Who among the following does NOT take part in the election of the President of India?
explanation_en: Under Article 54, only elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the State and UT (Delhi, Puducherry) Assemblies vote. Nominated members do not.

question_en: Under which Article is the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
explanation_en: Article 64 makes the Vice-President ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States. Article 66 deals with the election of the Vice-President.

subtopic: Polity – Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
question_en: The 91st Amendment (2003) limits the size of the Union Council of Ministers, including the PM, to what share of the Lok Sabha's total strength?
explanation_en: Article 75(1A), added by the 91st Amendment, caps the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha's total members. The same Amendment also tightened the anti-defection law.

question_en: Who decides whether a bill is a Money Bill?
explanation_en: Under Article 110(3) the Speaker's decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final. The Speaker endorses a certificate on it before it goes to the Rajya Sabha.

question_en: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament cannot be called to resolve a deadlock on which bill?
explanation_en: Article 368 requires each House to pass an Amendment Bill separately, so a joint sitting is not possible. A joint sitting is also not available for a Money Bill.

question_en: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha submits a letter of resignation to:
explanation_en: Under Article 94, the Speaker resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker. The Deputy Speaker in turn resigns to the Speaker.

question_en: Under Article 85, the gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot be more than:
explanation_en: Article 85 requires Parliament to meet at least once in six months. In practice there are three sessions: Budget, Monsoon and Winter.

question_en: Under which Article can Parliament create or abolish a State Legislative Council after the State Assembly passes a resolution?
explanation_en: Article 169 lets Parliament create or abolish a Council if the Assembly passes a resolution by special majority. Such a law is not treated as an amendment under Article 368.

question_en: The 74th Amendment added which Schedule listing 18 subjects for municipalities?
explanation_en: The 74th Amendment (1992) added Part IX-A and the Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects. The 73rd Amendment added the Eleventh Schedule for panchayats.

question_en: Under the 73rd Amendment, what minimum share of seats in Panchayats is reserved for women?
explanation_en: Article 243D reserves at least one-third of seats and chairperson posts in Panchayats for women. Many states have raised this to 50%.

question_en: The Finance Commission, which recommends sharing of central taxes with states, is set up under:
explanation_en: Article 280 provides for a Finance Commission every five years or earlier. It recommends how tax proceeds are divided between the Union and the States.

question_en: Which Article directs the Union to promote the spread and development of the Hindi language?
explanation_en: Article 351 is the directive for development of Hindi. Article 343 makes Hindi in Devanagari the official language of the Union.

question_en: The 44th Amendment (1978) replaced the words 'internal disturbance' as a ground for National Emergency with:
explanation_en: After the 1975 Emergency, the 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352. It also required the Cabinet's written advice for a proclamation.

question_en: The 103rd Amendment (2019) providing reservation for Economically Weaker Sections inserted which clauses?
explanation_en: Articles 15(6) and 16(6) allow up to 10% EWS reservation in education and public jobs. The Supreme Court upheld it in Janhit Abhiyan (2022).

question_en: The Election Commission of India is provided for under which Article?
explanation_en: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission. It conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President.

question_en: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed under which Article?
explanation_en: Article 148 provides for the CAG, appointed by the President. The CAG holds office for six years or until age 65, whichever is earlier.

question_en: Which writ asks a person 'by what authority' he holds a public office?
explanation_en: Quo Warranto stops a person from illegally holding a public office. Mandamus means 'we command' and Certiorari quashes orders of lower courts.

question_en:
Consider the statements:
I. A High Court can issue writs under Article 226 for enforcing Fundamental Rights and also for 'any other purpose'.
II. The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.
Which is/are correct?
explanation_en: Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights and other legal rights, so it is wider than Article 32. Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right, while Article 226 is not.

question_en: The collegium system of appointing judges originated from which case?
explanation_en: The Second Judges Case (SC Advocates-on-Record Association, 1993) gave primacy to the CJI and senior judges. The 1998 case widened it to the CJI plus four senior judges.

question_en: Financial Emergency can be proclaimed by the President under which Article?
explanation_en: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency, which has never been declared. Article 352 covers National Emergency and Article 356 President's Rule.

question_en: Under Article 239AA, the Delhi Legislative Assembly cannot make laws on which of the following?
explanation_en: Article 239AA, inserted by the 69th Amendment, keeps public order, police and land outside the Assembly's powers. These subjects stay with the Centre.

question_en: In which case did a nine-judge bench hold in 2017 that the right to privacy is a Fundamental Right?
explanation_en: The Puttaswamy judgment held privacy to be part of Article 21 and Part III. Maneka Gandhi (1978) had earlier widened the meaning of Article 21.
